method: BME Design Ch. 6: critical-spec gate (6.5.1), weighted decision matrix (6.4.2) with predefined rubric (6.4.4), decision support matrix with rotated datums (6.4.3, 6.7), House of Quality (6.4.5), weight-sensitivity analysis

names.A: Concept A - Integrated alert + forecast + intervention response

criteria.name: Regulatory and development risk (low risk = high score)

C1.5: Real-data sensitivity >= 0.90 AND warns >= 10 s earlier than a conventional monitor
C1.4: Real-data sensitivity >= 0.85 AND warns earlier than a conventional monitor (> 0 s)
C1.3: Real-data sensitivity >= 0.80 (marginal spec), no earlier than a conventional monitor
C1.1: Sensitivity < 0.50, or no real-time detection at all

C2.5: Minimal hazard: not time-critical, cannot falsely reassure in real time
C2.4: Gate handles >= 99 % of faults AND under-alerts < 1 % of critical-hypotension time (ALARP)

C4.5: No real-time alarms, or <= 1 false alarm per patient-hour with specificity >= 0.90
C4.4: <= 3 false alarms per hour with specificity >= 0.85
C4.3: <= 6 false alarms per hour, or specificity >= 0.80
C4.1: > 12 false alarms per hour, or alarming most of the time (WATCH specificity < 0.5)

C5.5: Real-time alerts + explanations + treatment response with agreement >= 0.90
C5.4: Real-time alerts + explanations + treatment response with agreement >= 0.75
C5.3: Real-time measured values and alarms, no prediction or treatment response
C5.2: Low-confidence real-time estimate only, or retrospective insight only

C6.5: Invasive and non-invasive settings, or any setting with monitor data
C6.4: Any setting with stored monitor records (retrospective)

C7.5: Exportable episode report (printable + data export) and full timeline

C8.5: No new development or clearance (existing cleared product)
C8.4: Lower-risk retrospective decision support; simpler validation
C8.3: Class II with a predicate (Hypotension Prediction Index, DEN160044 -> 510(k))
C8.2: Class II with new claims and no supporting performance evidence

DATUM.C1: real-data sensitivity 0.95; reactive by definition (lead 0 s)
DATUM.C2: under-alert during true MAP<55: 0.003; established, well-characterised risks
DATUM.C3: current measured MAP as a 15 s predictor: MAE 2.64 mmHg (persistence)
DATUM.C5: measured values and threshold alarms; no prediction or treatment response
DATUM.C6: continuous MAP alarms need an arterial line
DATUM.C8: existing cleared product - nothing to develop

A.C1: real-data sensitivity 0.96; AUROC synthetic 0.9847, real 0.9551; lead vs conventional monitor 2.0 s (DETERIORATING), 2.0 s (WATCH)
A.C2: faults handled 1.00; under-alert during true MAP<55: 0.003
A.C5: real-time alerts with plain-language reasons, forecast, R/C trends; treatment-response agreement 0.96
A.C6: requires an arterial line (ICU / operating room)
A.C7: event log during the session; no export
A.C8: Class II; predicate exists (Hypotension Prediction Index, 21 CFR 870.2210); three subsystems to validate

B.C1: real-data sensitivity 0.00; AUROC synthetic 0.6744, real 0.591; lead vs conventional monitor None s (DETERIORATING), 2.5 s (WATCH)
B.C2: faults handled 1.00; under-alert during true MAP<55: 1.000
B.C5: low-confidence estimate capped at WATCH; no treatment response
B.C6: ECG + PPG only: step-down, recovery and lower-resource settings
B.C7: event log during the session; no export
B.C8: Class II with new non-invasive claims that current evidence does not support

C.C2: retrospective, not time-critical: cannot falsely reassure in real time
C.C3: same model pipeline as A: real-patient MAE 4.695 mmHg (synthetic 4.525)
C.C6: any setting with stored monitor records
C.C7: printable report with charts + CSV + JSON export, full timeline
C.C8: still a device (processes physiological signals) but retrospective and lower risk

roof.why: More sensitive alerting raises alarm burden
Accurate forecasts enable earlier, correct alerts

notes: + C3/C1: Accurate forecasts enable earlier, correct alerts
+ C2/C1: Fail-safe floor/hold controls protect detection
- C1/C4: More sensitive alerting raises alarm burden
+ C3/C4: Accurate forecasts reduce false alarms

rationale: Critical-specification gate (6.5.1): only A meets every must-meet (*) specification. B fails SPEC-01, SPEC-02, SPEC-06, SPEC-15; C fails SPEC-02 (a retrospective tool cannot detect deterioration at the bedside, which is the problem statement).
Weighted decision matrix: A 3.95, C 3.60, B 2.00, current practice 3.70 of 5 (House of Quality adjusted A 4.15).
Scoring uncertainty (6.4.4): A stays ahead of C under each single pessimistic re-scoring (4 of 4); only if all four judgements go against A at once does C edge ahead (3.85 vs 3.65).

Weight sensitivity is the weak point: C wins 66% of 10,000 random weightings and the equal-weight case, because C is low-risk and documents well. With the other weights kept in their base proportions, A wins once early detection (C1) carries >= 9.5 % weight; the project need puts it at 20 %.
Discrimination: AUROC 0.98 simulated / 0.96 real for A vs 0.67 / 0.59 for B.
Real-patient accuracy 4.7 mmHg MAE against the arterial line.
Safety after risk controls: 100% of signal faults handled; under-alert during critical hypotension 0.3% (Version 5 alone: 53%).
Treatment response tracked in real time with 96% agreement (unconfounded events).

Honest limit: on real patients A warns earlier than a conventional monitor at 46% of onsets (mean +8.7 s, median 0.0 s) and detects 2 onsets the monitor misses; the 15 s forecast horizon caps the lead time, and A is only modestly ahead of current practice overall.

Benchmark against persistence (Ch. 4.4): carrying the current measured MAP forward 15 s is MORE accurate overall (2.12 vs 4.27 mmHg simulated; 2.64 vs 4.7 mmHg real); the model is better only while pressure is changing > 5 mmHg in 15 s (8.54 vs 9.97 mmHg) - which is when an early warning matters. A longer forecast horizon is the main design iteration.

Recommendation (recombination, Ch. 6): adopt A and fold C's review/report in as A's documentation module (fixes A's C7 score); keep B as a future research concept until non-invasive accuracy improves.
